projectBackground.name: Parcelwise Signup Release
projectBackground.context: The signup form accepts ages 18 to 65. The last release shipped with a boundary bug and customers noticed.

manager.name: Marek Zielinski
manager.note: Tests are only useful if someone else can reproduce them. Be specific.

assignment.title: Test the signup release
assignment.brief: Choose boundary tests, compute coverage and defect density, and write a reproducible bug report.

documents.name: Requirements
documents.note: Age must be between 18 and 65 inclusive.

documents.name: Defect Log
documents.note: 24 defects found in 12 thousand lines of code.

tasks.title: Boundary Values
tasks.prompt: Valid ages are 18 to 65 inclusive. Which set best tests the boundaries?
tasks.reasoning: Boundary testing checks values on and next to each limit.
tasks.tip: Test just below, on and just above each boundary.
tasks.mistake: Mid-range values rarely find boundary bugs.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Defect Density
tasks.prompt: 24 defects were found in 12 KLOC (thousand lines of code). What is the defect density per KLOC?
tasks.mistake: Raw counts mislead when code size differs.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Execution Coverage
tasks.prompt: 180 of 240 planned test cases were executed. What percentage of planned tests ran?
tasks.reasoning: Execution coverage shows progress against the plan.
tasks.tip: Report what was not run and why.
tasks.mistake: Reporting only passes hides unexecuted tests.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Bug Report Fields
tasks.prompt: Select the fields a good bug report includes.
options: The tester's opinion of the developer
tasks.reasoning: Reproducibility needs steps, expectation and environment.
tasks.tip: Write it so a stranger can reproduce it.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Regression Testing
tasks.prompt: After a bug fix, why run regression tests?
options: To confirm existing behaviour still works
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Test Summary
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence test summary for the release manager.
tasks.modelAnswer: We executed 180 of 240 planned tests (75%) and found 24 defects, a density of 2 per KLOC. The age boundary at 65 accepted 66, which is a high severity defect and blocks release. Sixty tests remain, mostly payment edge cases; I recommend completing them before go or no-go. Regression tests on signup passed after the fix.
tasks.reasoning: A good summary has status, key risk, what's left and a recommendation.
tasks.mistake: Reporting only totals hides the decision-relevant defect.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Boundary Bug
caseStudy.background: A promotion allowed ages 18-65 but accepted 66. Eight thousand users signed up outside the target, voiding an insurer's coverage and costing £60,000.
caseStudy.constraints: Boundary tests were not in the plan.
questions: How do you make them routine?
caseStudy.solution: Forge added boundary tests to the standard test template.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Test the edges; that's where defects live.

quiz.q: Case study bug was missed because:

prompts: How do you decide what to test first?
What makes a bug report useful?
When would you block a release?
